Nagaland is known as the 'Land of Festivals', and its best-known — the Hornbill Festival — runs every year from 1 to 10 December at the Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima.

Kohima, the capital of Nagaland, lies at an average elevation of 1,261 m. It saw one of the fiercest battles fought on Indian soil in World War II, remembered at the War Cemetery on Garrison Hill.

overview.text:
Imphal is best visited between October and April; November brings the Sangai Festival and March the five-day Yaoshang, the Manipuri Holi.

Kangla Fort, the old royal seat, stands at its heart; the Ima Keithel is run entirely by women.

overview.text:
Mizoram — the 'land of the hill people' — borders Myanmar and Bangladesh. It became a Union Territory in 1972. Mizo society runs on Tlawmngaihna, a code of hospitality and unselfishness.

Aizawl is the capital; Reiek, Dampa, Champhai and Murlen, the 230 m Vantawng Falls and Phawngpui, the highest peak, are the main draws.

items.body: Ujjayanta Palace: Ujjayanta Palace, built by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya and named by Rabindranath Tagore, has three domes up to 86 feet and now houses the Tripura State Museum.

items.title: Tripura

Elsewhere in Tripura — Neermahal: Neermahal, built from 1930 by Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya on Rudrasagar Lake at Melaghar, is India's largest water palace, designed by Martin & Burns.

guides.seoDescription: Hornbill Festival guide: 1–10 December at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, tribal dances, morungs, wrestling and games, permits and planning.

body.intro: Nagaland's 'festival of festivals' fills Kisama every December.

sections.heading: When and where
sections.text: Every year from 1 to 10 December at the Kisama Heritage Village, about 12 km from Kohima. The Government of Nagaland has run it since 2000.

sections.heading: What you'll see
sections.text: Tribal dances in the 16 morungs, crafts and food stalls, Naga wrestling, and games like fire-making, archery and stone-pulling.

sections.heading: Plan around it
sections.text: Fly to Dimapur, which also serves Kohima; get your Inner Line Permit first. Add Khonoma or the Dzükou trek.

body.intro: Loktak is a lake that floats — its phumdis even carry a national park.

sections.heading: Loktak Lake
sections.text: The largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, at Moirang — 250 to 500 sq km by season — and a Ramsar site since 1990.

sections.heading: Keibul Lamjao
sections.text: About 53 km from Imphal: the world's only floating national park, 40 sq km of phumdis, set up to protect the Sangai deer. Guided boats run through it.

sections.heading: Nearby
sections.text: The INA Memorial at Moirang marks the Indian National Army's first hoisting of the Indian flag.
